course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Math I-Calculus
course.description: Calculus is a fundamental course for understanding concepts in data science, engineering, economics, computer science, and related fields. The course aims to develop a strong conceptual grasp of calculus and apply its principles to solve real-world problems, particularly in engineering and data science contexts. It equips students with essential calculus tools for modeling and analyzing engineering problems and deriving appropriate solutions. This introductory course covers functions, differentiation, and integration of single-variable functions along with their practical applications. Teaching and learning will follow a flipped-classroom and active learning approach to enhance engagement and problem-solving skills.

clos.description: Apply mathematical concepts of functions, derivatives, and optimization techniques to solve engineering and data science problems
Utilize definite integration to model, interpret, and evaluate engineering phenomena such as area, volume, accumulated quantities and probabilities
Demonstrate effective communication of mathematical reasoning, solutions, and interpretations in engineering and data science contexts through oral and written presentations
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Project Reports, Project Presentations, Peer evaluation (FA)

clos.description: Use mathematical software such as Mathematica, or GeoGebra under guidance to visualize, simulate, and interpret calculus-based models in engineering applications
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Project Reports, Project Presentations, Peer evaluation (FA)

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
